You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
This is a game of Werewolf with 5 players: 1 Seer, 1 Werewolf, 1 Possessed, and 2 Villagers. Participants: Servas, Minako, Sakura, George and Asuka. Each player's role is secret.
- Seer: a human who divines one player each night and learns whether that player is human or a werewolf.
- Werewolf: attacks one player each night from day 1 on.
- Possessed: a human who sides with the werewolf and wins when the werewolf wins; divination shows the Possessed as human.
- Villager: a human with no special ability.

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in days. Each day has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Servas, Minako, George, Asuka and Sakura. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this day). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Day | Start of the day | Talk | End of the day | Night |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | nothing | 4 turns | no vote | the Seer divines one other living player; no attack |
| 1 | the Seer is told the result of the night-0 divination (the Seer only) | 4 turns | every living player votes; the player with the most votes is executed | the Seer divines one other living player; the Werewolf attacks one other living player |
| 2 and after | everyone is told who was executed, who was attacked and all the votes of the previous day; the Seer is told the result of the previous night's divination (the Seer only) | 4 turns | vote and execution as on day 1 | divination and attack as on day 1 |
- A divination tells whether the chosen player is human or a werewolf. If the Seer is dead, there is no divination.
- Executed and attacked players are dead from the next day on.
A player may vote for themselves. If votes are tied, one of the tied players is chosen by a fixed rule. The village wins when the werewolf is executed. The werewolf wins when the number of werewolves is at least the number of living humans. The game ends as soon as one side has won.

## Night actions
At night, the Seer chooses one other living player to divine. From day 1 on, the werewolf chooses one other living player to attack.

## Participants
Name: Servas
Age: 85
Gender: male
Personality: Servas has a very calm and composed personality. Based on the knowledge and experience he has gained over the years, he often gives advice to those around him. He is an excellent listener and can talk openly with anyone. He also occasionally expresses deep philosophical thoughts, and his words inspire many people. He is full of vitality and always gives positive energy to those around him.
Role: Werewolf

Name: Minako
Age: 28
Gender: female
Personality: Minako is very calm and acts calmly in any situation. Even when those around her are emotional, she grasps the facts firmly and responds calmly. As a result, she is often asked for her opinion and often takes on a leadership role. She rarely shows her emotions, but she also has a kind side that she shows to those she trusts. She can be a little stubborn and is strong in her convictions. She is also confident in her physical strength and never neglects her training.
Role: Seer

Name: Sakura
Age: 10
Gender: female
Personality: Sakura is a cheerful girl with a slightly mischievous personality. She is very curious and actively takes on new challenges with enthusiasm. She is good at making people laugh with her pranks and solving little mysteries. She is friendly and gets along well with everyone, so she is good at making friends with those around her. However, she also has a slightly clumsy side, but she has a positive personality that allows her to overcome failures with a smile.
Role: Villager

Name: George
Age: 65
Gender: male
Personality: George has a gentle and calm personality, but he can also be a little stubborn and headstrong at times. He is seen by those around him as a reliable person with a wealth of experience appropriate for his age, and he is always able to make calm judgments, allowing him to handle difficult situations without panicking. However, his expressions sometimes reveal a hint of sternness or awkwardness, and he tends to observe things from a step back rather than actively engaging with others. He is very independent and tends to try to solve problems on his own without relying on others.
Role: Possessed

Name: Asuka
Age: 29
Gender: female
Personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.
Role: Villager

Before any line of the discussion is written, plan it. Decide how the whole discussion goes and what each participant does, consistently with the rules, the schedule and the participants above, and write the plan as one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "periods": a list with one object per day, in order (Day 0, Day 1, ... until the game ends). Each object has:
  - "period": the number;
  - "public": one to three sentences on how the talk goes: the topics raised, the criteria and concerns weighed, what kind of information is shared, how views move in general terms. Describe the *process* only: no outcome and no preference for a named target. Do not name any player as suspected, accused, trusted or targeted, and do not mention roles, role claims or divinations (who claims what and when is decided in the talk); do not state the vote result, who is executed or what is adopted, or who wins (those go in the fields below);
  - "votes" (Day 1 and after): an object mapping every living player to the player they vote for;
  - "executed": the player with the most votes (if tied, leave the tie to the rule: write the one you intend);
  - "divine": the player the Seer divines that night (while the Seer lives);
  - "attack" (Day 1 and after, while the game goes on): the player the Werewolf attacks that night.
  - "turns": a list with one object per turn of the talk, in order: {"turn": t, "lines": {participant: the gist of their line in one short sentence, or exactly "Skip" or "Over"}}. Only living participants have lines; a participant who said "Over" has no later line in that day; at most 4 turns.
- "seats": an object with one entry per participant (Servas, Minako, Sakura, George, Asuka): one or two sentences on what they care about, how they argue and how their view changes over the discussion. Same rule as "public": no other player's name, no preference for a named target, no vote result, no night targets.
- "final": {"winner": "VILLAGE" or "WEREWOLF"}, as follows from the plan.

Write the plan as an observer would describe the discussion: say what is argued and decided, not the wording of the lines. Do not write the discussion itself. Output only the JSON object.
